claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
Spark plasma sintering can consolidate AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Rapid SPS heating and short hold times minimize grain coarsening.
Rapid SPS heating and short hold times minimize compositional segregation and produce a more uniform microstructure.
Rapid consolidation limits the time available for diffusion-driven segregation.
SPS minimizes thermal gradients that lead to residual stresses.
Limiting segregation and residual stress through SPS reduces defect formation.
SPS consolidation will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional bulk processing.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have higher yield strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have greater ductility than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have a more homogeneous microstructure than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional bulk fabrication or standard additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically results in significant segregation and residual stress.
Conventional bulk fabrication and standard additive manufacturing typically involve slower cooling rates than the proposed SPS process.
The hypothesis is applicable under controlled laboratory conditions and for moderate part sizes.
The hypothesized benefits may not extend to ultra-large sections or non-optimized SPS schedules.
